**Practical notebook.** Follow homology classes through a controlled
filtration. <a href="../../downloads/topic-04-participant.ipynb" download="topic-04-participant.ipynb">Download the notebook</a>.

Persistent homology treats the complexes in a filtration as related, not as
unconnected pictures. Move the scale control slowly: individual marks,
intermediate groups and large organisation become visible over different
ranges rather than at one privileged resolution.

Here a **topological feature** means a homology class followed through the
filtration: a component class in $H_0$, a loop class in $H_1$ or a cavity
class in $H_2$.

::: {.column-margin .study-note .qualification}
**Analogy, not a persistence calculation.** Blurring makes the multiscale idea
visible, but persistent homology does not recognise letters. It applies
homology to nested complexes and follows components, loops or cavities as the
scale changes.
:::

At each scale $a$, homology records the features in $K_a$. Persistent homology
also records what those features become when the scale increases from $a$ to
$b$:

$$
H_p(K_a;\mathbb F)\longrightarrow H_p(K_b;\mathbb F),
\qquad a\leq b.
$$

Here $p$ is the homology dimension: $p=0$ for components, $p=1$ for loops and
$p=2$ for cavities. The detailed treatment makes the arrow precise.

::: {.checkpoint-route}

The checkpoint is to explain why homology computed independently at several
scales is not yet persistent homology: the relationships across scale are also
part of the object.

:::
